result.topic_en: Latin draft for the Paris prize problem on heat conduction: when the reduced equation is free of differential quotients with respect to β, the solution u takes the form ap+bq+c or ap+b, and in the case m=2 one concludes that either ΔΛ=θΔ or u is composite.
result.transcription:
Pariser Aufgabe. 9.

inter functiones $Q$ et $n-\mu$ aequationes inter functiones $P$, quarum coeffi-
cientes sint functiones solius $\beta$, denotante $\mu$ quempiam numerorum $0, 1 \dots n$.
Obtinebuntur igitur expressiones ipsarum $\frac{\partial q}{\partial t}$ per quotientes differentiales
ipsarum $q$ secundum $\beta$ ab ipsa $\alpha$ liberae.
  Iam casus singulos problematis nostri ad hunc casum pertinentes
perlustremus.
  Quando $m=2$ et $\Delta$ est formae $\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta + e\partial_\alpha + f\partial_\beta$ aequatio reducta $\Delta\Lambda u$
$=0$, si a quotientibus differentialibus secundum $\beta$ libera evadit, formam
induet
$$\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\alpha^3} + r\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha} = 0$$
unde $u$ erit formae
$$ap + bq + c$$
denotantibus $a, b, c$ functiones solarum $\beta$ et $t$, $p$ et $q$ autem functio-
nes solarum $\alpha$ et $\beta$. Iam in locum ipsius $\alpha$ variabilis independens $q$
introduci potest. Quo pacto obtinetur
$$u = ap + \alpha b + c$$
ubi jam sola $p$ est functio ambarum variabilium $\alpha$ et $\beta$. Substituendo
hanc expressionem in aequationibus
$$\Delta u = 0, \quad \Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$$
coefficientium formae facile eruuntur (coefficientes harum aequationum
facile per functionem $p$ exprimuntur. Sed hoc hic non persequemur,
quum hic casus in corporibus homogeneis occurrere nequeat).
  Restat casus, quando jam una aequationum, in quas aequatio $F=0$
discinditur, formam (1) habet ideoque formam
$$r\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha} = 0$$
Tum erit
$$u = ap + b$$
denotantibus $a$ et $b$ functiones solarum $\beta$ et $t$, et $p$ functionem sola-
rum $\alpha$ et $\beta$. Si in locum ipsius $\alpha$ variabilis independens $p$ introduci-
tur, prodibit
$$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2} = 0$$
[Invenimus igitur, si $m=2$ sive aequatio $F=0$ in duas aequationes
$$\Delta u = 0, \quad \Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$$
dissolvatur, esse aut $\Delta\Lambda = \theta\Delta$, aut functionem $u$ compositam esse

methods.what: When the coefficients depend only on β, the equations yield expressions for ∂q/∂t in terms of β-derivatives of q that are free of α
methods.quote:
Obtinebuntur igitur expressiones ipsarum $\frac{\partial q}{\partial t}$ per quotientes differentiales
ipsarum $q$ secundum $\beta$ ab ipsa $\alpha$ liberae.

methods.what: Reduced equation ΔΛu=0, free of β-derivatives, becomes a third-order linear ODE in α; its solution is linear in two functions p and q
methods.quote:
$$\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\alpha^3} + r\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha} = 0$$
unde $u$ erit formae
$$ap + bq + c$$

methods.what: Change of independent variable from α to q simplifies the solution
Second-order case: solution u=ap+b; taking p as the independent variable reduces the equation to ∂²u/∂α²=0
Result for m=2: either ΔΛ=θΔ or u is composite

items.english: Now let us survey the individual cases of our problem that belong to this case.

items.english: The forms of the coefficients are easily derived (the coefficients of these equations are easily expressed through the function p. But we shall not pursue this here, since this case cannot occur in homogeneous bodies).

items.quote:
Invenimus igitur, si $m=2$ sive aequatio $F=0$ in duas aequationes
$$\Delta u = 0, \quad \Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$$
dissolvatur, esse aut $\Delta\Lambda = \theta\Delta$, aut functionem $u$ compositam esse
items.english: We have therefore found that if m=2, i.e. if the equation F=0 splits into the two equations Δu=0, Λu=∂u/∂t, then either ΔΛ=θΔ or the function u is composite.
